title: Microsoft Purview: permanently delete OneDrive and SharePoint files with Priority cleanup (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
notes: claim 85: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the briefing says the cmdlets run in Security & Compliance PowerShell, but Microsoft requires Exchange Online PowerShell for audit searches. The permanent-deletion path also omits a policy-type choice in the wizard. The roadmap facts, licensing list and main deletion safeguards are supported.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft plans a hard-delete configuration for Priority cleanup policies targeting OneDrive and SharePoint files that skips recycle bins.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The roadmap describes retention policies and labels keeping ODSP data in Recycle Bins for 93 days to prevent inadvertent data loss.
claims.quote: To help prevent inadvertent data loss, M365 retention labels policies and M365 retention policies do not hard delete content immediately and keeps the data in Recycle Bins for 93 days for ODSP.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes hard delete as costly because misconfiguration can cause data loss and legal implications.
claims.quote: Hard delete itself is a very costly process as it opens Microsoft to heavy legal implications in case of any data loss incident that may occur due to a misconfigured policy or regression.

claims.claim: The roadmap description does not say existing deletion behaviour changes automatically on arrival.
claims.quote: Ability to select hard delete configuration for a Priority cleanup policy for OneDrive and SharePoint content and skip recycle bins.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Permanent deletion is an additional Priority Cleanup option that bypasses the OneDrive and SharePoint recycle bins.
claims.quote: This option bypasses the SharePoint and OneDrive recycle bins. ... Permanent deletion is an additional option for a Priority Cleanup policy.

claims.claim: Deleted content is no longer discoverable in SharePoint search, Microsoft 365 Copilot or eDiscovery.
claims.quote: After deletion, the content is no longer discoverable in SharePoint search, Microsoft 365 Copilot, or eDiscovery.

claims.claim: The standard Priority Cleanup workflow moves identified items to the second-stage Recycle Bin.
claims.quote: Use the standard Priority Cleanup workflow when you want identified items to move to the second-stage Recycle Bin.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters
claims.claim: Permanent deletion is admin-opt-in: an administrator must configure and explicitly select it, and deletion requires approval.
claims.quote: Create a Priority Cleanup policy and explicitly select the permanent deletion option. ... After all required approvals are complete, the selected items bypass the recycle bins and are permanently deleted.

claims.claim: The tenant switch is in Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup settings > Configuration > control for priority cleanup.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management. ... From the top right, select Priority cleanup settings. ... From the Configuration page, turn off the control for priority cleanup, and select Save.

claims.claim: No automation for the tenant-level Priority cleanup switch is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: '"priority cleanup" "tenant" "PowerShell" disable configuration'; 'Priority cleanup disable tenant configuration PowerShell permanent deletion PriorityCleanup RetentionComplianceRule license'. Opened priority-cleanup-onedrive-sharepoint and New-RetentionCompliancePolicy; only UI found.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Priority Cleanup Admin is required to create and manage SharePoint/OneDrive policies and enable or disable the feature.
claims.quote: For SharePoint and OneDrive, this role is required to create and manage priority cleanup policies, and enable or disable the feature.

claims.claim: Turning off Priority cleanup at the tenant level affects Exchange as well as SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: When you turn off priority cleanup, you're turning it off for Exchange as well as for SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.claim: Existing policies continue working after the tenant switch is turned off, while new policies cannot be created.
claims.quote: New priority cleanup policies can't be created until you turn on the control and select Save again. ... Existing priority cleanup policies continue to function

claims.claim: Existing policies cannot be modified while the tenant switch is off.
claims.quote: Existing priority cleanup policies can't be modified

claims.claim: Existing policies can be deleted while the tenant switch is off.
claims.quote: Existing priority cleanup policies can be deleted

claims.claim: Priority cleanup itself is enabled by default at the tenant level.
claims.quote: Because of the built-in safeguards, the feature itself is enabled by default at the tenant level.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Priority Cleanup Admin is automatically added to the Organization Management role group.
claims.quote: This role is automatically added to the Organization Management role group but must be manually added to any other role group.

claims.claim: Priority Cleanup Admin must be added manually to other role groups.
claims.quote: This role is automatically added to the Organization Management role group but must be manually added to any other role group.

claims.claim: Priority Cleanup Viewer provides visibility of policies and settings without allowing changes or policy creation.
claims.quote: Alternatively, the Priority Cleanup Viewer role allows only the visibility of priority cleanup policies and settings without the ability to make changes or create new policies.

claims.claim: Policy creation starts at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup > + Create a priority cleanup.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal and go to Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup. ... Select + Create a priority cleanup.

claims.claim: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Name <policy name> -PriorityCleanup creates a Priority cleanup policy.
claims.quote: The Name parameter specifies the unique name of the retention policy. ... The PriorityCleanup switch specifies whether to create a Priority cleanup policy. You don't need to specify a value with this switch.

claims.claim: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy runs in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: The New-RetentionCompliancePolicy reference does not document how this call selects permanent deletion.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Priority cleanup" "permanent deletion" PowerShell RetentionComplianceRule API'. Opened New-RetentionCompliancePolicy and searched its text for PriorityCleanup and permanent; it documents PriorityCleanup and SkipPriorityCleanupConfirmation, not a permanent-deletion selector.

claims.claim: The permanent-deletion path goes directly from + Create a priority cleanup to Choose what to do with the content > Delete data permanently without a policy-type choice.
claims.quote: For Choose the type of priority cleanup, select Adaptive or Static then select Next. ... For Static scope, select Policy for SharePoint/OneDrive and then select one or more of the locations for sites and OneDrive accounts.
claims.fix: Give an explicitly static route in controls[2].ui.path and the rendered table: 'Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup > + Create a priority cleanup > Choose the type of priority cleanup > Static > Policy for SharePoint/OneDrive > Tell us what you're looking for > Choose what to do with the content > Delete data permanently'. The type and workload choices are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/priority-cleanup-onedrive-sharepoint; the final page and option are documented at the existing permanent-deletion URL. State in the row note that this is the static-scope route.

claims.claim: No scripted operation selecting the SharePoint/OneDrive permanent-deletion option is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Priority cleanup" "permanent deletion" PowerShell RetentionComplianceRule API'. Opened priority-cleanup-permanent-deletion, New-RetentionCompliancePolicy, New-RetentionComplianceRule and Set-RetentionComplianceRule; no documented recycle-bin-bypass selector found.

claims.claim: Policies support adaptive or static scopes and SharePoint or OneDrive locations.
claims.quote: Enter the policy name and description, choose an adaptive or static scope, select the SharePoint or OneDrive locations, and define the query for the targeted files.

claims.quote: If an approver doesn't agree to delete an identified item, they must assign an existing retention label (any configuration) to the item.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup cannot target items marked as records or regulatory records.
claims.quote: You can't use priority cleanup for items that are marked as a record or regulatory record.

claims.claim: PriorityCleanupFileDeleted indicates that Priority Cleanup permanently deleted an item.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: No licensing statement specific to the permanent-deletion option, as distinct from Priority cleanup policies generally, is published.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Priority cleanup" "permanent deletion" licensing requirements'. Opened priority-cleanup-permanent-deletion, priority-cleanup-onedrive-sharepoint and Microsoft Purview service description; the licensing passage covers Priority cleanup labels generally, not this option separately.

claims.claim: Microsoft presents SharePoint/OneDrive Priority cleanup as a way to reclaim storage from files such as stale Teams meeting recordings and transcripts.
claims.quote: Delete stale Teams meeting recordings and transcripts, turned on for Copilot recap ... To reclaim the space from these files, or any other similarly large files that don't need to be retained as long as your retention policies, you can take action to remove them.

claims.claim: Approvers review identified items on the Pending cleanups page.
claims.quote: On the Pending cleanups page, items identified by a priority cleanup policy are listed with a status of Pending disposition ... When the approver selects one of the list items, the next page shows them the individual items with the item names, locations, and senders.

claims.claim: The permanent-deletion page gives no completion time after final approval.
claims.quote: Searched: '"priority cleanup" "permanent deletion" completion timing GCC GCC High DoD'. Read priority-cleanup-permanent-deletion in full; it states deletion follows approvals but no completion interval. The Exchange timing results concern mailboxes, not this option.

claims.claim: The standard SharePoint/OneDrive workflow page says to allow up to seven days for deletion.
claims.quote: Items that are approved or relabeled are then moved to the Disposed items tab. Allow up to seven days for items to be deleted.

claims.claim: The governance checklist tells readers to manage controls that have no corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote: Review membership of the Organization Management role group ... Turn on auditing ... Assign approver roles ... Run simulation ... Tell approvers which existing retention labels are suitable ... Review the policy list
claims.fix: The Before rollout steps for Organization Management membership, enabling auditing and assigning approver roles have no table row. The At rollout steps for simulation/turning on policies and choosing fallback retention labels also have no row; neither does After rollout policy-list/deletion management. This is a checklist/table coverage finding, not a request to add rows.

claims.claim: End users see only a retention label named after the policy on identified files.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Priority cleanup" SharePoint OneDrive permanent deletion "end user" retention label experience'. Opened priority-cleanup-onedrive-sharepoint and priority-cleanup-permanent-deletion; they document the label and deletion, not that the label is the only end-user effect.
claims.fix: Remove 'only': 'End users see a retention label named after the policy on files it identifies.' This wording is supported by https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/priority-cleanup-onedrive-sharepoint. The low impact rating itself is not a blocker.

claims.claim: One Priority cleanup policy cannot cover Exchange, SharePoint and OneDrive together.
claims.quote: As a result of these differences, you can't create a cleanup policy for all three locations in same policy.
